title: Homogeneity Auditing as a Deployment Requirement

original_idea.title: Homogeneity Auditing as a Deployment Requirement
original_idea.problem: There are no standards or practices requiring organizations deploying multiple AI systems to audit inter-system output diversity before deployment.
original_idea.direction: Propose and prototype a lightweight homogeneity audit protocol: sample outputs from all deployed models on a fixed probe set, compute pairwise semantic similarity, flag portfolios above a concentration threshold.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Without mandatory audit practices, systemic risk from correlated failures accumulates invisibly until a large-scale failure event occurs.
original_idea.relevant_context: MIT 2025 report found 95% of GenAI pilots stall; understanding whether homogeneity contributes to this failure rate is unexplored.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: proposing audit protocols is useful, but the actual safety impact depends on adoption by organizations, which is uncertain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: implementing a prototype audit tool with semantic similarity computation and threshold detection is feasible for CS students with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a prototype audit protocol with probe set, similarity computation, and concentration threshold is a concrete, bounded tool.

novelty.reasoning: AI audit frameworks exist (ISACA 2024, TrustArc 2025) but focus on bias, fairness, and compliance rather than inter-model output diversity. IOSCO (2025) flags concentration risk in financial AI but does not propose a specific homogeneity audit protocol. The Artificial Hivemind identifies the homogeneity problem but does not propose deployment-stage auditing tools. The specific proposal for a lightweight probe-set-based homogeneity audit with concentration thresholds is mostly novel as a practical tool.
